classification.difficultyReason: Read each labelled radius, square it inside the radical and select the root sign from the graph's orientation; no inference beyond the standard semicircle form is required.

content.prompt: Write down the equation of the following semi-circles.

spec.description: Upper semicircle, labelled intercepts −3 and 3 and maximum 3; no grid or point markers.

answer.worked:
The radius is $3$ and the semicircle lies above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{3^2-x^2}\\y&=\sqrt{9-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Lower semicircle with endpoint labels ±sqrt(3) and minimum −sqrt(3); no grid.
spec.mathematics: Origin-centred lower semicircle of radius sqrt(3).

answer.worked:
The radius is $\sqrt3$ and the semicircle lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2-x^2}\\y&=-\sqrt{3-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper semicircle with stacked fraction labels −1/5, 1/5 and maximum 1/5; no grid.

answer.worked:
The radius is $\frac15$ and the semicircle lies above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{\left(\frac15\right)^2-x^2}\\y&=\sqrt{\frac1{25}-x^2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Lower semicircle with stacked fraction labels ±3/2 and minimum −3/2; no grid.

answer.worked:
The radius is $\frac32$ and the semicircle lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\sqrt{\left(\frac32\right)^2-x^2}\\y&=-\sqrt{\frac94-x^2}\end{align*}$$
